status: Fixed before first candidate outcome measurement
question: Can agreement between the two predicted corners qualify stricter box suppression and preserve a neighboring partial front that box-only suppression removes?
motivation: The completed additional IoU 0.60 restriction removes duplicates but loses an incomplete front in the reviewed-label model. RMPE motivates comparing poses when identifying redundant detections. This is a separate two-corner project rule, not a reproduction of its learned multi-joint distance.
input: Completed original-view output populations with existing two-view averaged coordinates from the immutable R68 result archive. The R68 reflected-output union is excluded.
candidate: Process outputs by descending original box confidence and ascending original output index for ties. Remove a same-class candidate only when a previously kept output has box IoU strictly above 0.60, both records each have two accepted corners, and both corresponding left-left and right-right Euclidean distances are at most 5 original-image pixels.
accepted_corner: Finite x and y, 0 <= x < 1280, 0 <= y < 720, and original corner confidence at least 0.50. No availability or coordinate is inferred from a reference label.
geometry: Use the existing completed corner coordinates in the original image frame. Preserve all survivor boxes, scores, coordinates, classes, identities and relative output order. Do not recompute cross-view associations or averages.
threshold_basis: IoU 0.60 is the previously measured stricter-output control. Five pixels is the existing strict corner tolerance, reused as a declared heuristic for prediction agreement. Neither value is tuned using the candidate result.
evaluation: Fresh unchanged confidence-ordered matching at reference IoU at least 0.50. Report all misses, extras, duplicate subset, zero/one/two-known groups, known-corner outcomes, complete-pair success, empty-image outputs, gains, losses and rematches.
scope: Exploratory fixed rule on the same development photographs. Predicted corner agreement can preserve a shared error. A two-corner requirement can also leave duplicates with unavailable corners untouched.
